1.why: Body text uses a clean sans-serif with comfortable letter and line spacing, though secondary text such as the mock provisioning URI and Logs entries is small, gray, and tightly packed.

2.why: No italics or all-caps prose appear anywhere, but the step-4 testing note is a multi-line block of continuous text that is mildly dense.

3.why: All screens use a single-column mobile-width layout with large touch targets, but the provisioning URI on step 4 overflows its card and log text wraps awkwardly.

4.why: Each step carries a single short plain-language instruction, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code currently displayed by your authenticator app.'

5.why: Expected input formats are illustrated via placeholders and demo values ('Six digits', 'ABCDE-23456', demo email and password in the step-1 callout), though the code fields describe rather than exemplify the actual value.

6.why: All mandatory instructions are one or two lines; the longer callout notes are supplementary and never required to proceed.

7.why: The manual secret sits in a selectable text field and recovery codes are rendered as selectable text so they can be copied, but no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code appears on any screen; step 3 explicitly tells the user to 'add it manually', offering only a plain-text mock provisioning URI that is not scannable or clickable.

9.why: Standard labeled email, mobile and password inputs are shown, but autofill or password-manager support cannot be confirmed or refuted from the screenshots alone.

10.why: Every screen shows a 'Step X of 5' chip, a large heading, and one prominent full-width blue primary button.

11.why: Each enrolment screen asks for exactly one action (Continue, Verify identity, Generate, Confirm, Save codes); the extra options on the settings page are styled as muted secondary actions.

12.why: Actions are confirmed with plain banners ('Recovery code accepted and consumed.', 'You have been logged out.', 'Authenticator app protection is active.'), but what comes next is conveyed by navigation to the next screen rather than stated in text.

13.why: Retry is invited ('Please try again') and recovery codes can be regenerated, but there is no reveal/hide control, no SMS resend option, and regeneration invalidates all previous codes.

14.why: The only observed error, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', does not state what the problem is, though it suggests retrying and does not blame the user.

15.why: Step 4 explicitly states 'This setup expires in five minutes' and authenticator codes rotate every 30 seconds, so time limits are imposed on reading and code entry.
